openQuestions.text: What does the hook brief actually put in front of a model today, and can a model on each of the six CLIs act on it without guessing the command id, its policy, the document to read and whether it was already offered?
Which command-discovery surface defects (the g5 `skill.md` collision and its siblings) keep a command from being offered or found on each runtime, and what detects them before a user hits one?

keyFindings.text: The cold-start caps on the two sides of the shim disagree, and the tighter one wins. The shim passes the advisor child a 2200 ms budget (`CHILD_TIMEOUT_MS` 2500 minus a 300 ms start margin) and kills it at 2500 ms, while the CLI may wait up to 5000 ms for a cold daemon before its local fallback answers. The hub vocabulary is paraphrase-blind: it matches the phrasing used in the corpus rows that already pass and misses ordinary rewordings of the same task.
